setups.title: OpenAI Agents SDK
setups.snippet:
from agents import Agent, Runner
from agents.mcp import MCPServerStreamableHttp

async with MCPServerStreamableHttp(
    name="Polarion",
    params={
        "url": "https://YOUR-SERVER/mcp",
        "headers": {"Authorization": "Bearer YOUR_POLARION_PAT"},
    },
) as server:
    agent = Agent(name="Polarion assistant", mcp_servers=[server])
    result = await Runner.run(agent, "List Polarion projects")
setups.note: Use inside your async application with openai-agents installed and Agent imported from agents. Run the agent while the server context is open. Keep API keys and PATs in your application secret store.

setups.note: This uses the REST wrapper and its HTTP_API_KEY, not the MCP endpoint or the user PAT. The reduced schema contains 30 actions. A team administrator deploys the REST wrapper first.

setups.title: Docker team server
setups.snippet:
docker run -d --name polarion-mcp \
  -p 127.0.0.1:3000:3000 \
  -e API_BASE_URL=https://polarion.company.example/polarion/rest/v1 \
  -e MCP_ALLOWED_HOSTS=localhost:3000,127.0.0.1:3000 \
  ghcr.io/phillipboesger/polarion-mcp:1.4.5
setups.note: The image starts Streamable HTTP at http://localhost:3000/mcp. Each caller sends their own Polarion PAT. For team access, proxy HTTPS to the loopback port, forward the public Host, and add your public hostname to MCP_ALLOWED_HOSTS. Cloud connectors also need OAuth; their Docker choice includes that configuration.

setups.title: REST wrapper / OpenAPI
setups.snippet:
docker run -d --name polarion-rest \
  -p 127.0.0.1:3000:3000 \
  -e API_BASE_URL=https://YOUR-POLARION/polarion/rest/v1 \
  -e BEARER_TOKEN=YOUR_POLARION_PAT \
  -e HTTP_API_KEY=YOUR_WRAPPER_API_KEY \
  -e PUBLIC_URL=https://YOUR-SERVER \
  -e TRUST_PROXY=1 \
  ghcr.io/phillipboesger/polarion-mcp:1.4.5 \
  node build/http-server.js
setups.note: All calls use the deployment PAT. Clients send Authorization: Bearer <HTTP_API_KEY>. Serve this behind HTTPS; schemas are at /openapi.json and /openapi-gpt.json. Forward the public Host through your TLS proxy. HTTP_API_KEY is a random secret you invent (for example from openssl rand -hex 32); callers send it as the Bearer token. TRUST_PROXY=1 lets the 100-requests-per-15-minutes limit count each caller separately behind your proxy.

setups.title: n8n HTTP Request
setups.snippet:
curl -X POST https://YOUR-SERVER/api/tools/getCurrentUser \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${HTTP_API_KEY}" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{}'
setups.note: This setup uses the REST wrapper. Its administrator configures API_BASE_URL, BEARER_TOKEN and HTTP_API_KEY. Store the wrapper key in an n8n credential after importing.

setups.title: HTTPS team server with OAuth
setups.snippet:
docker run -d --name polarion-mcp \
  -p 127.0.0.1:3000:3000 \
  -e API_BASE_URL=https://polarion.company.example/polarion/rest/v1 \
  -e MCP_ALLOWED_HOSTS=YOUR-SERVER \
  -e MCP_PUBLIC_URL=https://YOUR-SERVER \
  -e MCP_TOKEN_SECRET=YOUR_RANDOM_SECRET_AT_LEAST_32_CHARS \
  -e MCP_ALLOWED_REDIRECT_PRESETS=claude \
  -e TRUST_PROXY=1 \
  ghcr.io/phillipboesger/polarion-mcp:1.4.5
setups.note: Put a TLS reverse proxy at https://YOUR-SERVER in front of 127.0.0.1:3000 and forward the public Host. TRUST_PROXY=1 assumes exactly one trusted proxy hop; adjust it to your network. Generate a stable secret of at least 32 characters. The claude redirect preset allows the claude.ai callback used by Claude web and Desktop connectors.

clients.summary: Claude app on your computer.

steps: Update Claude Desktop first (Claude menu > Check for Updates...) and check node --version in a terminal.
Open the Claude menu in the system menu bar (not the settings inside the Claude window), then Settings... > Developer.

Click Edit Config. This creates claude_desktop_config.json if it does not exist: macOS ~/Library/Application Support/Claude/claude_desktop_config.json, Windows %APPDATA%\Claude\claude_desktop_config.json.
Add the polarion entry inside mcpServers, or paste the whole snippet.
Replace YOUR-POLARION and YOUR_POLARION_PAT, then save the file.
Quit Claude Desktop completely and start it again.
In a new chat, click the + indicator (Add files, connectors, and more) in the input box, move over Connectors and check that polarion is listed under Manage connectors.
local.note: Local servers run with your user permissions and use your local network. They work only in Claude Desktop, not in claude.ai or Cowork, and Advanced research cannot call their tools. Claude asks for approval before each tool call.

Node.js 22+ (node --version works in a terminal)

Read mcp-server-polarion.log in the log folder above, check API_BASE_URL and the PAT, then restart Claude Desktop.

steps: Get the server address (https://YOUR-SERVER/mcp) from your administrator.

Go to Customize > Connectors (in Claude Desktop you can also reach it via the + indicator in the input box, Connectors > Manage connectors). On Free choose Add custom connector; on Pro/Max click + Add > Add custom connector. On Team/Enterprise only an Owner can add it (see the note below).

fails.symptom: "Couldn't reach the MCP server" or sign-in does not open
fails.fix: Claude connects from Anthropic's cloud, not from your device. The hostname must resolve from the public internet to a globally routable IPv4 address (an A record; private 10.x/172.16-31.x/192.168.x, 100.64.0.0/10, loopback or AAAA-only names are rejected). VPN, split-horizon DNS and firewalled servers fail; allow Anthropic's outbound range 160.79.104.0/21 in the firewall or WAF (look for 403 or 429 in edge logs). Enterprise organizations in a private network can request MCP tunnels (research preview).

Register the exact URL the server listens on: if https://YOUR-SERVER/mcp redirects (301, 302, 307, 308) to another host, Claude drops the Authorization header and the sign-in fails. If the error page URL shows a flow_id starting with ofid_, note it for a support report.

fails.symptom: Sign-in ends with a redirect_uri error
fails.fix: The administrator must set MCP_ALLOWED_REDIRECT_PRESETS=claude on the server.
The PAT was cut off, has expired or is for another Polarion. Create a new token and paste it unchanged.

fails.symptom: Connector shows Connect or Reconnect instead of Connected
fails.fix: Sign-in did not finish. Click it and sign in again. Authentication settings cannot be edited after adding: remove the connector and add it again, then reconnect.

server.teamNote: Team: only Owners and Primary Owners can add connectors; Enterprise: Owners, Primary Owners and custom roles with "Manage access to Libraries". clients.label: Claude Code
unverified: Windows native npx wrapper (cmd /c): not found in the Claude Code MCP page or the MCP quickstart; not included.

Whether a running Claude Code session picks up a server added with claude mcp add from another terminal: the quickstart says to run the command outside a session and use /mcp to check or reconnect; nothing documents hot-adding. .mcp.json is documented as read at session start.
Behaviour of http://localhost for the --transport http flag is not documented by the vendor (works as a plain URL; curl -I is the documented reachability check).
clients.summary: Claude in your terminal.

steps: Open a terminal in a project directory. Run the command outside a claude session.
Replace YOUR-POLARION and YOUR_POLARION_PAT in the command below, then run it. Options go before the server name; everything after -- is the server command.
Run claude mcp list. Wait a moment and run it again if polarion shows Failed to connect while npx downloads the package; it should show Connected.
Run claude and type /mcp to confirm polarion is connected.
local.snippet: claude mcp add --env API_BASE_URL=https://YOUR-POLARION/polarion/rest/v1 --env BEARER_TOKEN=YOUR_POLARION_PAT --transport stdio polarion -- npx -y polarion-mcp
local.note: The default scope is local: private to you and active only in the project where you ran the command (stored in ~/.claude.json). Add --scope user before the name to use it in all projects. Servers already in Claude Desktop can be copied with claude mcp add-from-claude-desktop (macOS and WSL).
needs: Claude Code installed and signed in
Node.js 22+

verify.prompt: Which Polarion user am I? Use getCurrentUser.
verify.expect: Claude shows your Polarion user. /mcp shows polarion as connected.

fails.fix: Claude Code is not installed or the terminal was not reopened after installing.
Local-scope servers belong to the project where you added them. Start claude in that project, or re-add with --scope user. Claude Code reads only ~/.claude.json and <project>/.mcp.json.

fails.symptom: /mcp or claude mcp list shows polarion as failed
fails.fix: Run claude mcp get polarion and check the command shown matches what you ran (a missing -- before npx changes it). Run the command in a terminal to see the error, check node --version (22+) and that API_BASE_URL ends in /polarion/rest/v1.
The first npx run can take longer than the 30 second startup limit. Start with MCP_TIMEOUT=60000 claude (PowerShell: $env:MCP_TIMEOUT = "60000"; claude).
Run claude mcp remove polarion (add --scope local or user if it exists in several scopes), then add it again.

fails.symptom: Server connects but no tools appear
fails.fix: Select polarion in /mcp to see its tools. An empty list usually means a missing variable: check that both --env values were passed.
The PAT was cut off, has expired or is for another Polarion. Create a new token and paste it unchanged.

clients.label: API
unverified: The page calls authorization_token an OAuth access token and says callers obtain and refresh it; it does not state the header form sent to the MCP server. That it arrives as Authorization: Bearer <value> is how this repo expects it.
Model name left as placeholder: the vendor example uses claude-opus-5-5 and lists supported models, which change often.
The doc does not state a limit on the number of mcp_servers per request.
clients.summary: Your own code calling the Claude Messages API.

local.reason: Only public HTTP servers work; local stdio cannot connect.

steps: Set ANTHROPIC_API_KEY to your Anthropic API key.
Add mcp_servers (type url, https:// URL, unique name, authorization_token) and one matching tools entry of type mcp_toolset; send header anthropic-beta: mcp-client-2025-11-20 (or betas in the SDK).
Replace YOUR_CLAUDE_MODEL with a model name from the Anthropic docs that supports the MCP connector (the vendor example uses claude-opus-5-5).
Send the request, for example with the curl command.
Look for mcp_tool_use and mcp_tool_result blocks in the response.
server.note: The MCP connector is in beta and not covered by zero data retention. Only tool calls are supported, and the server must be public HTTPS (Streamable HTTP or SSE). Every server in mcp_servers needs exactly one mcp_toolset. Polarion PATs are passed as authorization_token as is; the vendor expects OAuth tokens you obtain and refresh yourself. The newer header mcp-client-2026-09-15 (Claude API only) pins tool lists and may be sent instead; mcp_tool_listing blocks then appear first in the response.

steps: Run pip install openai and set OPENAI_API_KEY (use a model that supports the MCP tool; the vendor says most recent models do).
Copy the snippet into a Python file.
Replace https://YOUR-SERVER/mcp, YOUR_POLARION_PAT and YOUR-MODEL in the snippet.
Run the file. The response contains an mcp_list_tools item (the imported tools) and an mcp_approval_request.
Send a second request with previous_response_id and an mcp_approval_response that carries approve and the approval_request_id. Each approval covers one tool call.
Repeat the approval for each further tool call. Keep the mcp_list_tools item in the conversation so the API does not fetch the tool list again each turn.
server.note: The authorization value is not stored by the API: send it on every request that creates a response. Failed calls fill the error field of the mcp_call item (protocol errors, tool errors or connectivity errors). With store=true, data sent to MCP servers is logged for 30 days unless Zero Data Retention is on. Rate limits for the tool: 1000 RPM on the Build tier, 2000 RPM on Launch and Grow. No extra fee per tool call, only the tokens used. allowed_tools limits which tools are imported; require_approval also takes an object such as {"never": {"tool_names": [...]}}.
server.snippet:
from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI()  # reads OPENAI_API_KEY

tools = [{
    "type": "mcp",
    "server_label": "polarion",
    "server_description": "Polarion ALM: projects, work items, documents.",
    "server_url": "https://YOUR-SERVER/mcp",
    "authorization": "YOUR_POLARION_PAT",
    "require_approval": "always",
}]

resp = client.responses.create(
    model="YOUR-MODEL",
    tools=tools,
    input="Which Polarion user am I? Use getCurrentUser.",
)
print([i.type for i in resp.output])

Public HTTPS Polarion MCP server (Streamable HTTP or HTTP/SSE)

import asyncio
from agents import Agent, Runner
from agents.mcp import MCPServerStdio

async def main():
    async with MCPServerStdio(
        name="Polarion",
        params={
            "command": "npx",
            "args": ["-y", "polarion-mcp"],
            "env": {
                "API_BASE_URL": "https://YOUR-POLARION/polarion/rest/v1",
                "BEARER_TOKEN": "YOUR_POLARION_PAT",
            },
        },
        client_session_timeout_seconds=60,
    ) as server:
        agent = Agent(name="Polarion assistant", mcp_servers=[server])
        result = await Runner.run(agent, "Which Polarion user am I? Use getCurrentUser.")
        print(result.final_output)

asyncio.run(main())
steps: Run: pip install openai-agents (inside a virtual environment: python -m venv .venv, then source .venv/bin/activate or .venv\Scripts\activate on Windows), and set OPENAI_API_KEY (macOS/Linux: export OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-...; PowerShell: $env:OPENAI_API_KEY = "sk-...")

serverModes.label: Local (npm / npx)
serverModes.description: Your client starts the server on your computer (stdio). Needs Node.js 22+ and a Polarion token.

serverModes.label: Server (Docker)
serverModes.description: A server your client connects to by URL. Needs Docker to host it; cloud clients also need public HTTPS and OAuth.

faq.a: Local: your client starts the server on your computer with `npx`. Server: you host the server with Docker and the client connects by URL; claude.ai and ChatGPT need it. Custom GPT Actions and n8n use the REST wrapper on a server.

faq.q: How do I create a Polarion personal access token (PAT)?
faq.a: Polarion user page > Personal Access Token > name and expiry > Create Token. Copy it at once, it is shown only once. If the page says token generation is not allowed, your administrator must enable `com.siemens.polarion.rest.security.restApiToken.enabled=true`.

faq.q: Is my data safe? Which permissions apply?
faq.a: Polarion enforces the permissions of the token owner. Server mode uses each caller's own token and the server stores none. Tool results go to your AI provider, so your organization's data policies apply.

faq.q: Can I limit the server to read-only?
faq.a: Yes: set `MCP_READ_ONLY=1` and restart. Only read tools are exposed. In write-enabled sessions every write tool can preview with `dry_run: true`.

faq.q: My AI client says "Disconnected" or "Failed to connect".
faq.a: Local: run `npx -y polarion-mcp` in a terminal with the same values to see the real error (Node older than 22 and JSON typos are common). Server: open `https://YOUR-SERVER/health`, then read `docker logs polarion-mcp`.

faqMore.q: It says 401 "Polarion did not accept this token".
faqMore.a: The token was cut off, has expired, or belongs to another Polarion. Test the token with the `/metadata` request in the setup guide (docs/guides/local-npm.md or docs/troubleshooting.md) and create a new token.

faqMore.q: It says 403 "Polarion denied access".
faqMore.a: Polarion denied access. Check the user's license and REST or item permissions for the affected tool. On Polarion 2512+ the login check reads /metadata and needs no global REST GET permission. On 2506 it reads /projects, which does. A 403 during login is rejected.

faqMore.q: The connector login in claude.ai or ChatGPT fails or loops.
faqMore.a: Check `MCP_PUBLIC_URL` (exact https address, no path), the padlock, that the redirect preset or callback is allowed (`MCP_ALLOWED_REDIRECT_PRESETS=claude`; the log says `redirect_uri rejected`), and that `MCP_TOKEN_SECRET` did not change.

faqMore.q: Does HTTP/OAuth work with Polarion 2506?
faqMore.a: Yes. On 2512+ the login check calls GET /metadata and needs no global REST GET permission. 2506 has no /metadata, so the server reads GET /projects instead; that user must be allowed global REST GET. A 403 is never accepted. Tool access still follows your Polarion permissions.

faqMore.q: What does Bearer mean in an Authorization header?
faqMore.a: It is just the word Bearer, one space, then your token: `Bearer YOUR_POLARION_PAT`. Without the word Bearer the server answers 401.

faqMore.q: Where do I keep my token safely?
faqMore.a: In your personal client settings or an environment variable, never in a file inside a shared project or repository. Anyone who can read the file can act as you in Polarion. With the OAuth connectors you type the token only on the server's login page and the AI client never stores it.

faqMore.q: Which Polarion versions work?
faqMore.a: Live integration tests run against Polarion 2506, 2512 and 2606, including HTTP/OAuth. The full tool set is targeted at the newest release; 2506 and 2512 stay usable with the limits in Polarion versions. The tools are generated from a Polarion OpenAPI definition, which does not guarantee every operation on every release. Verify the operations you rely on against your own instance.

faqMore.q: Which AI clients can I use?
faqMore.a: Any client that supports MCP over stdio or Streamable HTTP. The setup guide above lists the tested paths for Claude, ChatGPT and Codex, Copilot Studio, VS Code, Gemini, Cursor, Windsurf and JetBrains. Other clients can use the generic stdio or HTTP entries, or the REST wrapper.

faqMore.q: It says 503 "Polarion could not be reached".
faqMore.a: The server got no usable answer from Polarion. Read the `Polarion token probe GET /metadata failed` line in `docker logs polarion-mcp`. Check that `API_BASE_URL` is the full `/polarion/rest/v1` URL and reachable from the MCP container (not `localhost` inside Docker). Use the container-side probe in docs/troubleshooting.md. `/health` only confirms the MCP server runs.

faqMore.q: Can claude.ai or ChatGPT connect to a server on my own laptop?
faqMore.a: The provider must reach the MCP endpoint over public HTTPS, so `http://localhost` does not work for claude.ai or ChatGPT. Polarion itself can stay private if the MCP container can reach it over your network or VPN. Desktop and command-line clients may use `http://localhost:3000/mcp`. Use a local stdio setup if you do not want to publish an endpoint.

faqMore.q: What is the difference between the ChatGPT connector and a Custom GPT?
faqMore.a: The ChatGPT connector speaks MCP and everyone signs in with their own Polarion token. A Custom GPT uses the separate REST wrapper with one shared key (`HTTP_API_KEY`), so every call runs as the one Polarion user whose token the wrapper holds.

faqMore.q: Certificate errors: the public HTTPS address does not work.
faqMore.a: For cloud connectors, ensure the MCP hostname resolves publicly, ports 80 and 443 reach the TLS proxy, and the certificate is valid for that hostname. Keep certificate verification enabled. A private Polarion hostname may still be used for the separate connection from the MCP container.

faqMore.q: My Polarion uses a company or self-signed certificate.
faqMore.a: Keep TLS verification enabled. Mount the company CA PEM into the MCP container and set `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS=/certs/ca.pem` (for example `-v /path/ca.pem:/certs/ca.pem:ro -e NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS=/certs/ca.pem`). For npm mode, set `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS` in the client environment. This adds trusted roots without disabling certificate checks.

faqMore.q: Should I use polarion-mcp@latest or a pinned version?
faqMore.a: The plain `npx -y polarion-mcp` can keep using an older copy from npm's cache. `polarion-mcp@latest` checks the registry at every start and picks up new releases, which can change the tool list without notice. `polarion-mcp@1.4.5` always runs exactly that release. Teams should pin and upgrade on purpose. To force a refresh, switch to `@latest` or a newer pinned version and restart the client.

faqMore.q: How do I update the Docker server?
faqMore.a: Choose the new tag on the GitHub package page, then run `docker pull ghcr.io/phillipboesger/polarion-mcp:NEWTAG`, `docker rm -f polarion-mcp`, and the same `docker run` command with the new tag. Keep `MCP_TOKEN_SECRET` unchanged so users stay signed in. With a team URL the administrator updates the server and you only reconnect.

faqMore.q: It says "Unsupported engine" or the Node version is too old.
faqMore.a: The package needs Node.js 22 or newer: `node -v` must print v22 or higher. Install the LTS from nodejs.org and open a new terminal; with nvm run `nvm install 22 && nvm use 22`. Desktop apps can use a different Node than your terminal, so install Node system-wide and fully restart the app. Docker avoids this because the image bundles Node 22.

faqMore.q: Windows: the client cannot start npx.
faqMore.a: Typical symptoms are `spawn npx ENOENT` or a server that never starts. Use `cmd` as the command with the arguments `/c`, `npx`, `-y`, `polarion-mcp`, because npx is `npx.cmd` on Windows. Backslashes in JSON paths must be doubled (`C:\\path\\ca.pem`). Restart the app completely after every change.

faqMore.q: Port 3000 is already in use.
faqMore.a: Change only the left number of the port mapping: `-p 127.0.0.1:3100:3000`, then use `http://localhost:3100/mcp` and set `MCP_ALLOWED_HOSTS=localhost:3100,127.0.0.1:3100`. Remove an old container with `docker rm -f polarion-mcp`. On macOS and Linux `lsof -i :3000` shows who uses the port; on Windows use `netstat -ano | findstr :3000`.

faqMore.q: It says 429 "Too many requests".
faqMore.a: The server limits requests per address. Behind a proxy set `TRUST_PROXY=1`, otherwise all users share one counter, then wait 15 minutes for the window to reset. The REST wrapper has a fixed limit per 15 minutes.

faqMore.q: Gemini CLI says it was replaced. Which tool should I use?
faqMore.a: Google's page says Gemini CLI was replaced by Antigravity CLI on 18 June 2026 for no-cost-tier and Google One users. If your Gemini CLI still runs, for example with an API key or a company license, the steps in this guide work. Antigravity CLI has its own setup that this guide does not cover yet.

faqMore.q: Windsurf now says Devin. Which steps do I follow?
faqMore.a: The vendor docs moved to docs.devin.ai and describe this configuration only for the legacy Cascade agent. If your tab uses the Devin Local agent, MCP servers are set up in Devin CLI config files, which this guide does not cover yet.

faqMore.q: The error says `request_rejected HTTP 400`.
faqMore.a: Polarion or a proxy in front of it refused the hostname in `API_BASE_URL`. Use the address your users open in the browser. For the Polarion Docker image, add the name (for example `host.docker.internal`) to `ALLOWED_HOSTS` on the Polarion container and recreate it. See "ALLOWED_HOSTS recipe" in docs/troubleshooting.md. `MCP_ALLOWED_HOSTS` is a different setting.

faqMore.q: Every call returns 404, or `/rest/v1` does not exist.
faqMore.a: The REST API is not enabled or the path is wrong. Open `https://YOUR-POLARION/polarion/rest/v1/swagger-ui` in a browser; it must load. `API_BASE_URL` has to end in `/polarion/rest/v1`. Ask your Polarion administrator to enable the REST API if the page is missing.

faqMore.q: The PAT page says token generation is not allowed, or my token stopped working.
faqMore.a: An administrator must set `com.siemens.polarion.rest.security.restApiToken.enabled=true` and restart Polarion before PATs exist. A token also stops working when it expires or is revoked. Create a new one and replace it in your client; never paste it into a chat.

faqMore.q: My client warns about too many tools (VS Code 128, Cursor, Windsurf 100).
faqMore.a: The full catalog has 284 tools. Set `MCP_TOOLSETS` (for example `work-items,documents`) or `MCP_TOOLS` on the server, add `MCP_READ_ONLY=true`, or use `MCP_MODE=discover`. In VS Code you can also untick tools in the tools picker.

faqMore.q: GitHub Copilot shows no MCP servers on Business or Enterprise.
faqMore.a: The organization policy "MCP servers in Copilot" is off by default. An organization or enterprise owner must enable it in the Copilot policies. Free and Pro plans are not affected by this policy.

faqMore.q: My network needs a proxy to reach Polarion.
faqMore.a: Set `HTTPS_PROXY` (for example `http://proxy.corp:3128`, credentials as `user:pass@` are allowed) and `NO_PROXY` (for example `.corp.example,localhost`) in the environment of the local server or the container. Only https:// Polarion URLs go through the proxy, using CONNECT. A 407 means the proxy credentials are wrong.

faqMore.q: My Ollama or other self-hosted model never calls the tools.
faqMore.a: The model must support tool calling; many small models do not. Pick one that does, enable native function calling for it in Open WebUI, and make sure the MCP URL is reachable from the Open WebUI container (use the container name, not `localhost`).
